source_rows.header:
lemma fourier_indicator_norm_le_card' {N : Nat} [NeZero N]
    (A : Finset (ZMod N)) (r : ZMod N) :
    ‖fourier (indicator A) r‖ ≤ A.card := by

private lemma fourier_natWeight_norm_le_mass {N : Nat} [NeZero N]
    (w : ZMod N → Nat) (r : ZMod N) :
    ‖fourier (fun x => (w x : Complex)) r‖ ≤ ∑ x, w x := by

private lemma theorem1013_fourier_norm_le_card {N : Nat} [NeZero N]
    {X : Type*} [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X]
    (D : MultifunctionDomain N X) (r : ZMod N) :
    ‖fourier (domainFibreCountFunction D) r‖ ≤ Fintype.card X := by

lemma lemma122_fourier_norm_le {N : Nat} [NeZero N]
    (g : ZMod N → Complex) (hg : DiscValued g) (r : ZMod N) :
    ‖fourier g r‖ ≤ (N : Real) := by

mathematical_reasoning.name: fourier_indicator_norm_le_card'
mathematical_reasoning.reason: Calls the earlier fourier_indicator_norm_le_card at Proofs00Basics:359. Both complete statements are identical apart from <= versus ≤ notation. The preceding theorem already has exactly the same N, NeZero N, A and r.

mathematical_reasoning.name: fourier_natWeight_norm_le_mass
mathematical_reasoning.reason: Expand the discrete Fourier sum and distribute the natural-to-real cast over the mass. The existing norm_sum_le bound simplifies termwise because every standard additive character has norm one and a natural complex cast has norm equal to its real cast.

mathematical_reasoning.name: theorem1013_fourier_norm_le_card
mathematical_reasoning.reason: First rewrite card X using the already imported theorem1013Parameters_sum_fibre_cards D. After casting the fibre sum to Real, norm_sum_le applies to the Fourier sum; unfolding the fibre-count function and the same norm-one/natural-cast identities produces exactly that total.

mathematical_reasoning.name: lemma122_fourier_norm_le
mathematical_reasoning.reason: Use existing norm_sum_le_of_le with constant bound one. Its pointwise hypothesis is precisely hg x after character norm one and scalar multiplication normalization; the sum of ones is N.

edge_cases: The original NeZero N premise remains. No prime, positive weight, nonempty support, or nonempty X premise is added. Empty supports, zero weights and empty X are covered by the original finite-sum statements; all original DiscValued and Fintype/DecidableEq hypotheses remain byte-exact.
